title: Toward Meaningful Transparency for AI Chatbots: Disclosing Persuasive Intent Reduces Persuasion
abstract: arXiv:2608.11794v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The growing role of AI-generated content and AI-enabled systems in public communication has led regulators to demand clear disclosure of content provenance and AI involvement. But the effects of such disclosures remain uncertain. We test two disclosure approaches in their impact on an AI chatbot's persuasive appeal. In a preregistered experiment, 1,500 UK adults held a short conversation with a persuasive chatbot about one of 60 policy issues. The chatbot was identical for everyone. We randomized the disclosure that people received: nothing (control), a prominent disclosure that they were interacting with an AI (T1), or that disclosure plus the chatbot's persuasive intent and instructions (T2). The chatbot shifted attitudes by 12.6 points on a 100-point scale in the control group. translated_title: 面向AI聊天机器人的有意义透明度：披露说服意图减少说服力
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.11794v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：AI生成内容和AI赋能系统在公共传播中日益增长的作用促使监管机构要求明确披露内容来源和AI参与情况。但这些披露的效果仍不确定。我们测试了两种披露方法对AI聊天机器人说服吸引力的影响。在一项预注册实验中，1500名英国成年人就60个政策问题之一与一个有说服力的聊天机器人进行了简短对话。聊天机器人对所有参与者相同。我们随机分配了参与者收到的披露信息：无（对照组）、显著披露他们正在与AI互动（T1）、或该披露加上聊天机器人的说服意图和指令（T2）。在对照组中，聊天机器人将态度在100分制量表上改变了12.6点。AI身份披露实际上与无披露效果相当，变化为13.1点，而额外意图披露则削减了说服力。
tldr: 本论文发现，仅披露AI身份不足以减少聊天机器人的说服力，而披露其说服意图能有效降低说服效果，揭示了透明度机制的关键在于意图披露而非身份披露。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that disclosing AI identity alone does not reduce chatbot persuasion, while disclosing its persuasive intent effectively decreases persuasion, highlighting that meaningful transparency hinges on intent disclosure rather than identity disclosure.
